mainTopic: Slaughtering קדשי קדשים on top of the מזבח: the views of רבי יוסי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and a משנה that supports רבי יוחנן
overview: The משנה asks about קדשי קדשים that were slaughtered on top of the מזבח. רבי יוסי says this counts as the צפון. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the northern half counts as צפון and the southern half counts as דרום. רבי יוחנן explains that for רבי יוסי the whole מזבח stands in the צפון. רבי זירא challenges this approach, and רב אסי answers that both תנאים learn their views from one פסוק, "וזבחת עליו את עולתיך ואת שלמיך". They argue over whether the whole מזבח, or only half of it, serves each kind of קרבן. The גמרא then works out what 'on the ground opposite them' means in רבי יוחנן's statement, and concludes that it is the spot where a shrunken מזבח used to stand. Finally, רבי זירא finds a משנה in תמיד about the second wood-pile that hints at רבי יוחנן's teaching. The גמרא begins to show that this משנה follows רבי יוסי, and the ברייתא it starts to quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Slaughtering the holiest offerings on top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a disagreement about קדשי קדשים slaughtered on top of the מזבח. רבי יוסי treats it as the צפון. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה divides the מזבח down the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: קדשי קדשים that someone slaughtered on top of the מזבח: רבי יוסי says it is as though they were slaughtered in the north. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: from the middle of the מזבח toward the south counts like the south, and from the middle of the מזבח toward the north counts like the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks what happens if the holiest offerings, which must be slaughtered in the north part of the courtyard, were slaughtered up on the מזבח itself. Two תנאים give different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי קדשים must be slaughtered in the צפון, so the question is whether the top of the מזבח counts as צפון. רבי יוסי says yes, the whole top counts as צפון. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says only the northern half counts; the southern half counts as דרום and would disqualify the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
The holiest category of offerings, which must be slaughtered in the north
The top of the altar
North, the required place for slaughtering קדשי קדשים
As though, as if

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole גמרא that follows tries to understand what each תנא holds about where the מזבח actually stands in the courtyard.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: slaughtering on top of the מזבח counts as the צפון. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: the northern half counts as צפון and the southern half counts as דרום.

steps.title: רבי יוסי holds the whole altar stands in the north
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי holds that the entire מזבח is located in the northern part of the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי used to say that the whole מזבח stands in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רבי יוסי's view in the משנה. According to him, the whole מזבח is physically in the north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבי יוסי's ruling into a fact about where the מזבח stands. If the whole מזבח is in the צפון, then slaughtering anywhere on top of it is slaughtering in the צפון.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
He used to say
The entire altar

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the whole מזבח is located in the northern part of the courtyard.

steps.title: Why did רבי יוסי say 'as though'?
steps.stepSummary: If the whole מזבח really is in the צפון, why did רבי יוסי say 'as though' it was slaughtered in the north?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'as though'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a problem with a word. 'As though' sounds like it was not really the north, but we just said the whole מזבח truly is in the north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כאילו usually means something is treated like X without actually being X. That seems to clash with רבי יוחנן's claim that the מזבח actually stands in the צפון.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is (the meaning of)

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of "as though"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה in light of רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי used the word כאילו if the מזבח truly stands in the צפון.

steps.title: The word 'as though' answers the requirement of 'on the side'
steps.stepSummary: One might think the פסוק 'על ירך המזבח' requires slaughtering on the ground next to the מזבח, not on top of it. רבי יוסי teaches that even on top it is valid, as though it were done in the proper northern spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that we need the slaughter to be 'on the side' of the מזבח, and that is missing here. So רבי יוסי teaches us that it is still valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about 'as though.' The word does not mean the place is not north; it deals with a different concern, being 'on the side' of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The top of the מזבח is truly in the צפון, but the פסוק says to slaughter 'על ירך המזבח', which sounds like next to it on the ground. רבי יוסי says the slaughter is valid even though that detail is missing, and 'as though' means it is treated like a normal northern slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken thought)
We require

It teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: 'As though' here does NOT mean the top of the מזבח is outside the צפון. It means the slaughter counts as valid even without the 'on the side' detail.

phrases.english: You might have said
we require "on the side" — and that is missing;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:11. 'On the side' sounds like on the ground next to the altar, not on top of it.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word כאילו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כאילו addresses the על ירך requirement: even though the slaughter was not beside the מזבח, it is valid, as if done in the normal northern place.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, the whole מזבח is in the צפון. 'As though' only teaches that slaughtering on top is valid even though it is not 'on the side' of the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי זירא: then does the other opinion hold the altar is half north, half south?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רב אסי: if רבי יוסי's view reflects where the מזבח stands, then רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה must hold that half the מזבח is in the צפון and half in the דרום?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב אסי: If so, according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, should we also say that half of the מזבח is in the north and half in the south?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes רב אסי's method onto the second opinion in the משנה. This sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי's ruling comes from the physical location of the מזבח, then רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's half-and-half ruling would mean the מזבח physically straddles north and south. רבי זירא is suggesting this leads to a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so (introduces a problematic result)
So too, also
Half of it
South

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה –
phrases.english: If that is so, according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda —

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּחֶצְיוֹ בְּצָפוֹן וְחֶצְיוֹ בַּדָּרוֹם?!
phrases.english: should we also say that half of it is in the north and half of it is in the south?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן's location-based explanation to the second opinion in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation (via רב אסי) that the משנה's rulings depend on where the מזבח physically stands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the same logic, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה would have to hold that the מזבח stands half in the north and half in the south, which leads to the problem in the next step.

steps.title: But רב אסי himself said the ground opposite is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: If you accept that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds half the מזבח is in the צפון, that conflicts with רב אסי's own report from רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees that slaughtering on the ground opposite the northern half is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say yes, that is so, wasn't it you who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees that if he slaughtered them on the ground opposite it, it is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא closes off the easy way out. He shows that רב אסי's own earlier quote from רבי יוחנן contradicts the idea that the northern half of the מזבח is in the צפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the northern half of the מזבח were truly in the צפון, the ground right next to it would also be צפון, and slaughtering there would be valid. Since רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disqualifies that spot, he must not hold the מזבח is in the צפון at all. So his half-north rule cannot come from the מזבח's location, and the location-based reading is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say

Agrees, concedes

steps.confusionAlert: The disqualified spot is the ground beside the northern half of the מזבח, not the top of the מזבח. The point is that the top is valid but the ground right next to it is not.

phrases.english: And if you would say that indeed it is so;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אַתְּ הוּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:

phrases.notes: 'Opposite it' means on the floor of the courtyard, right next to the northern half of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי; וְהָא אַתְּ הוּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי זירא's challenge by blocking the answer 'yes, half is north'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds half the מזבח stands in the צפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the northern half of the מזבח were in the צפון, the ground opposite it would be valid. Since רבי יוחנן says רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disqualifies it, he cannot hold the מזבח is in the צפון, so the location-based approach seems to fail.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's challenge: for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the ground beside the northern half of the מזבח is invalid, so his half-north rule cannot simply be about where the מזבח stands.

steps.title: Both views come from one verse
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי explains that רבי יוחנן means both תנאים learned from one פסוק. רבי יוסי says the whole מזבח works for עולה and for שלמים. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says half works for עולה and half for שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן means. Both of them learned from one verse: "And you shall slaughter upon it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings." רבי יוסי holds that all of it is for the עולה and all of it is for the שלמים. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that half of it is for the עולה and half of it is for the שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers רבי זירא's challenges. The disagreement is not about where the מזבח stands. It is about how to read a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי זירא assumed each view reflects the physical location of the מזבח, and that led to a contradiction. Now the argument moves to a different basis. The פסוק allows slaughtering on top of the מזבח, and the only question is how much of the מזבח each type of קרבן may use. This removes the contradiction from Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them learned from the same verse
And you shall slaughter upon it (on the מזבח)
Burnt offering. It must be slaughtered in the north.
Peace offerings. They may be slaughtered anywhere in the courtyard.
Half of it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two names. רבי יוסי says the WHOLE מזבח is fine for both. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says HALF for each.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer unlocks the whole סוגיא. Both views now come from a verse, not from a map of the courtyard.

phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yoḥanan means:

steps.terutzMaskana: Both views come from one פסוק. They argue over whether the whole מזבח or only half serves each type of קרבן.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says half and half
steps.stepSummary: If the whole מזבח worked for an עולה, which has the strictest place rules, it would be obvious that it also works for שלמים. So the verse's mention of שלמים must be teaching a split.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think the whole of it is valid for an עולה, then once the whole of it is valid for an עולה, do we even need to say that the whole of it works for שלמים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's half-and-half view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה must be slaughtered in the north, while שלמים may be slaughtered anywhere. So if the whole מזבח counted for the stricter עולה, it would obviously count for the easier שלמים. The extra mention of שלמים would then be pointless. It must therefore teach that each type of קרבן gets a different half.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind (if you thought)
Now (if this is so)
Is it necessary to say? (it is obvious!)
Valid

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כּוּלּוֹ לְעוֹלָה כָּשֵׁר

steps.raayaSupportSource: The mention of שלמים in the פסוק would be unneeded if the whole מזבח served the עולה

steps.title: How רבי יוסי explains the mention of שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the mention of שלמים was needed. Without it, we might think only an עולה, whose space on the ground is tight, may be slaughtered on the מזבח, but not שלמים, which have plenty of room.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יוסי? It was needed. You might have thought: it is the עולה whose place is cramped, so it may be slaughtered on top. But שלמים, whose place is not cramped, maybe not. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי answers the argument from Step 8, and gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי turns the logic around. Because the עולה has only the narrow northern area, we might think the Torah allowed the top of the מזבח just to give it more room. שלמים do not need extra room, so we might think they may not use the top. The verse mentions שלמים to rule that out, so the whole מזבח is valid for both.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? (how does he answer?)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי says the whole מזבח is valid for both. The mention of שלמים is not extra, because without it we would have limited the top of the מזבח to the cramped עולה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the mention of שלמים shows a split, half and half.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב אסי's statement from רבי יוחנן word for word. It is setting up a close look at what 'opposite them on the ground' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, this statement was used as a challenge. Now the גמרא quotes it again for a new reason: to figure out what case it is describing. The word גופא signals a return to a statement mentioned in passing.

steps.title: What ground could be opposite the altar?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי asks what 'on the ground opposite them' means. The base and ledge are part of the מזבח, and they are not on the ground anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדיפתי said to רבינא: What does 'on the ground opposite them' mean? If you say it means the cubit of the יסוד or the cubit of the סובב, those are part of the מזבח itself! Also, how can that be called 'on the ground'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי challenges the wording of the statement. He cannot find any real place that fits 'on the ground opposite the מזבח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obvious suggestion is the base or ledge that sticks out from the מזבח. That fails twice. First, they are part of the מזבח, so slaughtering there counts as slaughtering on the מזבח. Second, they are raised up, so they cannot be called 'ground'.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion the גמרא will reject
The base of the מזבח, a cubit-wide strip at the bottom
The ledge running around the middle of the מזבח
And furthermore: adds a second problem

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
What is 'on the ground opposite them'?
If we say the cubit of the base or the cubit of the ledge,
this itself is the altar!
And furthermore, what does 'on the ground opposite them' mean?
phrases.notes: The base and ledge are raised up, so they cannot be called 'ground'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the statement quoted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'on the ground opposite them' in רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only obvious places near the מזבח, the יסוד and the סובב, are part of the מזבח itself and are not on the ground.

steps.title: Tunnels under the altar would not work either
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the case is someone who dug tunnels under the מזבח and slaughtered inside them. A ברייתא teaches that a מזבח may not stand over tunnels, so that מזבח would not be valid at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he dug tunnels in the ground and slaughtered in them, is a מזבח like that valid? A ברייתא teaches: 'An altar of earth you shall make for Me': it must be attached to the earth. So one may not build it on top of tunnels or on top of arches.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא continues his challenge. He suggests one more possible case and knocks it down too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tunnels would put slaughtering 'in the ground' directly under the northern half of the מזבח. But a מזבח built over hollow space is not a valid מזבח, as the פסוק and the ברייתא teach. Then there is no proper מזבח to compare to, and the case makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: brings up a possible answer in order to reject it
Tunnels, hollow spaces dug under the ground
Arches, hollow spaces with a curved roof

phrases.english: And if you will say
that he dug tunnels in the ground and slaughtered in them,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי הָוֵי מִזְבֵּחַ?!
phrases.english: is something like this a valid altar?!
But it is taught in a baraita:
'An altar of earth you shall make for Me'
that it must be attached to the earth;
phrases.notes: Some versions say מאדמה (in round brackets); the corrected wording is באדמה, 'to the earth'.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִבְנֶנּוּ לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מְחִילּוֹת
phrases.english: so one may not build it on top of tunnels
nor on top of arches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge from Step 11 by rejecting a second possible case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'on the ground opposite them' means tunnels dug under the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מזבח built over tunnels is not valid, so this case cannot be what רבי יוחנן meant.

steps.title: The case is an altar that was made smaller
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the statement is needed for a case where the מזבח was shrunk, and someone slaughtered on the ground where its northern half used to stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he made the מזבח smaller.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real case that fits the words 'on the ground opposite them'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מזבח is made smaller, the spot where its northern part used to be becomes plain ground. That spot is truly 'ground', and it is not part of the מזבח anymore. רבי יוחנן teaches that even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says slaughtering there is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for: introduces the specific case a statement refers to
He made it smaller, reduced its size

steps.whatToRemember: 'On the ground opposite them' means the ground where the northern half of a shrunken מזבח used to stand. Even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says קדשי קדשים slaughtered there are invalid.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he made it smaller.
phrases.notes: The מזבח was shrunk, and someone slaughtered on the ground where its northern half used to be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of Steps 11 and 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No real ground could be 'opposite' the מזבח. The יסוד and סובב are part of it, and tunnels are not allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is ground that used to lie under the northern half of a מזבח that was later made smaller.

steps.title: רבי זירא: why don't we learn this in a משנה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks how רבי יוחנן's teaching could be correct if no משנה teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Is it possible that this teaching of רבי יוחנן is true, and we did not learn it in a משנה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's earlier statement about רבי יוסי. רבי זירא opens a search for a משנה that supports it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא assumes that an important rule like this should have a source in a משנה. His question sets up the next move, where the גמרא will try to find that source.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible? Expresses surprise
It is so, it is correct

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Is it possible that this teaching of Rabbi Yochanan is correct,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's statement from earlier: according to רבי יוסי, the whole מזבח stood in the north.

phrases.english: and we did not learn it in a mishna?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֶפְשָׁר אִיתָא לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion of Steps 10-13 and returns to רבי יוחנן's main statement about רבי יוסי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether some משנה teaches רבי יוחנן's statement that according to רבי יוסי the whole מזבח stood in the north.

steps.title: רבי זירא finds a משנה about the second wood-pile
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא searches and finds a משנה in תמיד about where the second wood-pile for the קטורת stood on the מזבח, and how many coals it held.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא went out, looked carefully, and found a source. We learned in a משנה: the כהנים picked out good fig-tree wood to set up a second wood-pile on the מזבח, used for the קטורת. It stood opposite the southwest corner, four אמות north of that corner. It held about five סאה of coals. On שבת it held about eight סאה, because that is where they burned the two bowls of frankincense from the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers his own question from step 14. He found a משנה that he thinks hints at רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, רבי זירא was surprised that no משנה seemed to teach רבי יוחנן's statement that, for רבי יוסי, the whole מזבח stands in the צפון. Now he brings a משנה that gives an exact spot on the מזבח for the second wood-pile: four אמות north of the southwest corner. The גמרא has not yet explained how this spot connects to רבי יוחנן. That question comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He looked carefully and found
The second wood-pile on the מזבח, whose coals were used for the קטורת
The incense offering
A measure of volume
A bowl, here holding the frankincense of the לחם הפנים
The showbread placed each week on the שולחן

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself does not mention רבי יוחנן or say that the מזבח stands in the צפון. The connection is not explained yet; the גמרא asks about it right away in the next step.

phrases.english: He went out, looked carefully, and found:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי זירא, who asked the question in the previous step.

phrases.english: as we learned in a mishna:
They picked out from there good fig-tree wood
phrases.notes: "From there" means from the supply of wood the כהנים were using for the מזבח.

phrases.english: to set up a second wood-pile for the incense;
opposite the southwest corner,

phrases.aramaic: מָשׁוּךְ מִן הַקֶּרֶן כְּלַפֵּי צָפוֹן אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת;
phrases.english: moved away from the corner toward the north by four cubits;
enough for about five se'ah of coals.
And on Shabbat:
enough for about eight se'ah of coals,
because there they would place

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי בְּזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
phrases.english: the two bowls of frankincense of the showbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question in step 14 by bringing a משנה that supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching that, according to רבי יוסי, the whole מזבח stands in the צפון
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה תמיד 2:5, which places the second wood-pile four אמות north of the southwest corner

steps.title: How does this משנה hint at רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what in this משנה actually points to רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the hint here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the משנה that רבי זירא found actually shows anything about רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only describes where the second wood-pile stood and how many coals it held. On the surface, it says nothing about the whole מזבח standing in the צפון. So the גמרא wants to know which detail is the hint.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign or hint, meaning the detail that points to the teaching

phrases.english: And what is the hint?
phrases.notes: He means: which part of this משנה shows רבי יוחנן's teaching?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the משנה from step 15 works as a support.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which detail of the משנה about the second wood-pile connects to רבי יוחנן's teaching

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: this משנה follows the view of רבי יוסי, and it starts to quote a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This משנה follows רבי יוסי, as a ברייתא teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer by saying the משנה matches רבי יוסי's opinion. It is setting up the next move: the ברייתא with רבי יוסי's words comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To see how the משנה hints at רבי יוחנן, we first need to know whose view it follows. The גמרא says it follows רבי יוסי. The ברייתא that comes next will explain his view and why it matters here.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: In other words, this משנה follows רבי יוסי's view.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 16 by saying the משנה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוסי. The full explanation comes from the ברייתא quoted next.
